title: Co-Neighbor Encoding Schema: A Light-cost Structure Encoding Method for Dynamic Link Prediction

problem.claim: Dynamic graph structure features change as the graph evolves, making repeated recomputation time-consuming because of high-order subgraph construction.

gap.claim: Existing memory-based dynamic graph learning methods store node hidden states, leaving a need for more efficient structure feature construction and updating.

contributions.claim: CNES stores structural information in memory to avoid redundant link-level feature recomputation.
CNES uses a hashtable-based memory to compress the adjacency matrix and support efficient structure feature construction and parallel vector-based updating.
CNES introduces Temporal-Diverse Memory for generating long-term and short-term neighbor structure encodings.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors distinguish CNES from existing memory-based dynamic graph learning by introducing hashtable-based memory and Temporal-Diverse Memory, and propose the CNE-N framework using these techniques.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report that extensive experiments on thirteen public datasets verify the method's effectiveness and efficiency.

narrative_sequence.summary: Structure encoding is presented as important for distinguishing links in graphs.
In temporal graphs, evolving structure makes repeated high-order subgraph construction costly.
CNES addresses the cost by storing information in memory and using compressed, parallelizable structure updates.
Temporal-Diverse Memory generates long-term and short-term neighbor structure encodings, and these techniques form the CNE-N framework.
Experiments on thirteen public datasets are reported to support effectiveness and efficiency.

unknowns: The abstract does not report quantitative effectiveness or efficiency results.
The abstract does not describe the datasets, baselines, computational costs, or evaluation protocol.
